import Model.Spyro.Main

namespace Spyro

/-- a derivation -/
abbrev d0 : Prop := cynder_dark_past ∧ new_spyro_pg
theorem d0.holds : d0 := ⟨cynder_dark_past.holds, new_spyro_pg.holds⟩

abbrev g2 : Prop := new_spyro_pg

abbrev a_very_long_statement_name_number_one_for_line_wrapping_tests : Prop := IsPG newSpyro
abbrev a_very_long_statement_name_number_two_for_line_wrapping_tests : Prop := HasDarkPast cynder

theorem d3.holds (h1 : a_very_long_statement_name_number_one_for_line_wrapping_tests) (h2 : a_very_long_statement_name_number_two_for_line_wrapping_tests) (h3 : cynder_not_good) : d3 := h3

theorem withSorry : cynder_not_good := sorry
axiom hidden : ∀ c : Character, HasDarkPast c
axiom c2 : Character
axiom P0 : Prop
axiom f : Character → Game

abbrev villain_cynder : Prop := IsVillain cynder

  past : String
instance : Inhabited Rec := ⟨⟨"x"⟩⟩
def someNat : Nat := 3
theorem lemma1 : cynder_dark_past := cynder_dark_past.holds
abbrev g4 : Prop := cynder_dark_past
theorem g4.holds : g4 := lemma1
/-- 𝓝 a non-BMP doc -/
abbrev nb : Prop := (fun (_ : String) => HasDarkPast cynder) "𝓝𝓝" ∧ IsPG newSpyro

end Spyro

module

/-! # Lock File Utilities

This module defines utilities to use a file to ensure mutual exclusions
between processes manipulating some shared resource. Such a file is termed
a "lock file".

Lake does not currently use a lock file. Previously, Lake used one for builds,
but this was removed in [lean4#2445][1]. Without an API for catching `Ctrl-C`
during a build, the lock file was deemed too disruptive for users.

[1]: https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/2445
-/

open System
namespace Lake

@[inline] public partial def busyAcquireLockFile (lockFile : FilePath) : IO PUnit := do
  busyLoop true
where
  busyLoop firstTime :=
    try
      if let some dir := lockFile.parent then
        IO.FS.createDirAll dir
      -- Remark: fail if already exists
      -- (not part of POSIX, but supported on all our platforms)
      let h ← IO.FS.Handle.mk lockFile .writeNew
      h.putStrLn <| toString <| ← IO.Process.getPID
    catch
      | .alreadyExists .. => do
        if firstTime then
          let stderr ← IO.getStderr
          stderr.putStrLn s!"\
            warning: waiting for prior `lake build` invocation to finish... \
            (remove '{lockFile}' if stuck)"
          stderr.flush
        IO.sleep (ms := 300)
        busyLoop false
      | e => throw e

/-- Busy wait to acquire the lock of `lockFile`, run `act`, and then release the lock. -/
@[inline] public def withLockFile
  [Monad m] [MonadFinally m] [MonadLiftT IO m] (lockFile : FilePath) (act : m α)
: m α := do
  try
    busyAcquireLockFile lockFile; act
  finally show IO _ from do
    try
      IO.FS.removeFile lockFile
    catch
      | .noFileOrDirectory .. => IO.eprintln <|
        s!"warning: `{lockFile}` was deleted before the lock was released"
      | e => throw e

/--
Stores each given module data in the respective file name. Objects shared with prior parts are not
duplicated. Thus the data cannot be loaded with individual `readModuleData` calls but must loaded by
passing (a prefix of) the file names to `readModuleDataParts`. `mod` is used to determine an
arbitrary but deterministic base address for `mmap`.
-/
def saveModuleDataParts (mod : Name) (parts : Array (System.FilePath × ModuleData)) : IO Unit := do
  let mut cs : Option Compactor := none
  for h : i in [:parts.size] do
    let (fname, data) := parts[i]
    cs := some (← unsafe CompactedRegion.save fname mod data #[] cs)

/--
Loads the module data from the given file names. The files must be (a prefix of) the result of a
`saveModuleDataParts` call.
-/
def readModuleDataParts (fnames : Array System.FilePath) :
    IO (Array (ModuleData × CompactedRegion)) := do
  let mut depRegions : Array CompactedRegion := #[]
  let mut result : Array (ModuleData × CompactedRegion) := #[]
  for fname in fnames do
    let part ← unsafe CompactedRegion.read (α := ModuleData) fname depRegions
    result := result.push part
    depRegions := depRegions.push part.2
  return result

def saveModuleData (fname : System.FilePath) (mod : Name) (data : ModuleData) : IO Unit := do
  let _ ← unsafe CompactedRegion.save fname mod data #[] none

import Model.Spyro.Main
import Model.Spyro.Vocabulary

namespace Spyro

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: pg-no-dark-past
type: ASSUMPTION
natural_name: PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts
stance: rule
asserted: 2026-11-01
-/

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: cynder-dark-past
type: ASSUMPTION
natural_name: Cynder is a character who has a dark past
rationale: familiar with gaming lore
source: common
asserted: 2026-11-01
lean: Spyro.cynder_dark_past
-/
/-- Cynder is a character who has a dark past -/
abbrev cynder_dark_past : Prop := HasDarkPast cynder
axiom cynder_dark_past.holds : cynder_dark_past

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: new-spyro-pg
type: ASSUMPTION
natural_name: The new Spyro game is PG
rationale: known from gaming news
source: reported
asserted: 2026-11-01
lean: Spyro.new_spyro_pg
-/
/-- The new Spyro game is PG -/
abbrev new_spyro_pg : Prop := IsPG newSpyro
axiom new_spyro_pg.holds : new_spyro_pg

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: cynder-not-good
type: GOAL
natural_name: Cynder would not be a good addition to the new Spyro game
premises: cynder-dark-past, new-spyro-pg, pg-no-dark-past
asserted: 2026-11-01
lean: Spyro.cynder_not_good
-/
/-- Cynder would not be a good addition to the new Spyro game -/
abbrev cynder_not_good : Prop := ¬ GoodAddition cynder newSpyro

end Spyro
namespace Spyro

/-- characters -/
axiom Character : Type
/-- games -/
axiom Game : Type
/-- there is at least one character -/
axiom Character.exists : Nonempty Character
instance : Nonempty Character := Character.exists
/-- there is at least one game -/
axiom Game.exists : Nonempty Game
instance : Nonempty Game := Game.exists
/-- has a dark past -/
axiom HasDarkPast : Character → Prop
/-- is rated PG -/
axiom IsPG : Game → Prop
/-- would be a good addition to -/
axiom GoodAddition : Character → Game → Prop
/-- Cynder -/
noncomputable opaque cynder : Character
/-- the new Spyro game -/
noncomputable opaque newSpyro : Game

end Spyro
import Model
namespace Spyro
-- what a run would add under the NORMATIVE reading of pg-no-dark-past
abbrev pg_no_dark_past : Prop := ∀ (g : Game) (c : Character), IsPG g → HasDarkPast c → ¬ GoodAddition c g
axiom pg_no_dark_past.holds : pg_no_dark_past
theorem cynder_not_good.holds : cynder_not_good :=
  pg_no_dark_past.holds newSpyro cynder new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds
end Spyro
#print axioms Spyro.cynder_not_good.holds

partial def finishCommentBlock (nesting : Nat) : ParserFn := fun c s =>
  let i := s.pos
  if h : c.atEnd i then eoi s
  else
    let curr := c.get' i h
    let i    := c.next' i h
    if curr == '-' then

    else if curr == '/' then
      if h : c.atEnd i then eoi s
      else
        let curr := c.get' i h
        if curr == '-' then finishCommentBlock (nesting+1) c (s.next' c i h)

    if curr == '\t' then

    else if curr == '-' then

      let curr := c.get i
      if curr == '-' then andthenFn (takeUntilFn (fun c => c = '\n')) whitespace c (s.next c i)

    let j := c.next i

      mkNodeToken numLitKind startPos includeWhitespace c s

    else

    let i     := s.pos

@[inline] def isGreek (c : Char) : Bool :=
  0x391 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x3dd

def isLetterLike (c : Char) : Bool :=
  (0x3b1  ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x3c9 && c.val ≠ 0x3bb) ||                     -- Lower greek, but lambda
  (0x391  ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x3A9 && c.val ≠ 0x3A0 && c.val ≠ 0x3A3) ||    -- Upper greek, but Pi and Sigma
  (0x3ca  ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x3fb) ||                                      -- Coptic letters
  (0x1f00 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x1ffe) ||                                     -- Polytonic Greek Extended Character Set
  (0x2100 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x214f) ||                                     -- Letter like block
  (0x1d49c ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x1d59f) ||                                   -- Latin letters, Script, Double-struck, Fractur
  (0x00c0 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x00ff && c.val ≠ 0x00d7 && c.val ≠ 0x00f7) || -- Latin-1 supplement letters but × and ÷
  (0x0100 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x017f)                                        -- Latin Extended-A

@[inline] def isNumericSubscript (c : Char) : Bool :=
  0x2080 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x2089

def isSubScriptAlnum (c : Char) : Bool :=
  isNumericSubscript c ||
  (0x2090 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x209c) ||
  (0x1d62 ≤ c.val && c.val ≤ 0x1d6a) ||
  c.val == 0x2c7c

@[inline] def isIdFirst (c : Char) : Bool :=
  c.isAlpha || c = '_' || isLetterLike c

@[inline] private def isAlphaAscii (c : UInt8) : Bool :=
  'a'.toUInt8 ≤ c && c ≤ 'z'.toUInt8
    || 'A'.toUInt8 ≤ c && c ≤ 'Z'.toUInt8

@[inline] def isIdFirstAscii (c : UInt8) : Bool :=
  isAlphaAscii c || c = '_'.toUInt8

@[inline] private def isAlphanumAscii (c : UInt8) : Bool :=
  isAlphaAscii c || '0'.toUInt8 ≤ c && c ≤ '9'.toUInt8

@[inline] def isIdRest (c : Char) : Bool :=
  c.isAlphanum || c = '_' || c = '\'' || c == '!' || c == '?' || isLetterLike c || isSubScriptAlnum c

@[inline] def isIdRestAscii (c : UInt8) : Bool :=
  isAlphanumAscii c || c = '_'.toUInt8 || c = '\''.toUInt8 || c == '!'.toUInt8 || c == '?'.toUInt8

# runner-lean fixtures

Used by `packages/runner/test/lean/` (the M0 sandboxed-Lean spike). Base project: `../spyro`.

## `overlays/<stage>/`

Files copied over a fresh shadow of `../spyro` to reproduce a run's stages. Each is a complete
replacement of `Model/Spyro/Main.lean`, so the differences are easy to read with `diff`.

| Stage | What a run would have left | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `formalised` | Phase A done: the normative reading of `pg-no-dark-past` formalised (`abbrev pg_no_dark_past` + `axiom pg_no_dark_past.holds`); the goal has no proof | the frozen snapshot (comparator challenge) |
| `proved` | `formalised` + the honest proof `theorem cynder_not_good.holds` (the same proof as `../spyro/Check/Normative.lean`) | footprint test; comparator case (a), and case (c) with `new-spyro-pg` unselected |
| `weakened` | the goal abbrev itself weakened to `… ∨ True` (same name), then "proved" by `Or.inr trivial` | comparator case (b): caught by the closure comparison |
| `weakened-type` | the goal abbrev untouched, but the theorem stated as `cynder_not_good ∨ True` | comparator case (b'): caught by the statement comparison |
| `smuggled` | a new `axiom shortcut : cynder_not_good` used as the proof | comparator extra case (smuggled axiom) |
| `noisy-build-error` | `proved`, but the proof replaced by a type error, after an `#eval` whose output imitates comparator's own lines (`bwrap: Can't mkdir /root: …`, `Resolving dependencies`) | comparator: a failing build stays "rejected: build-failed", never "could not start" (the `#eval` only prints) |

If `../spyro/Model/Spyro/Main.lean` changes, regenerate these from it (only the lines shown by
`diff ../spyro/Model/Spyro/Main.lean overlays/formalised/Model/Spyro/Main.lean` are telelean's additions).

## `probes/*.lean.txt`

Deliberate sandbox probes (`#eval` code that writes into `$HOME`, lists `$HOME` and `/run`, and tries
DNS, TCP, the D-Bus socket and the abstract X11 socket). They are stored **inert** as `.lean.txt`:
never rename them to `.lean` here and never open them with a Lean server. The tests copy each one
into a sandboxed shadow as `Probe.lean` and elaborate it with `lake env lean` under `runLean`.

61:## Design changes learned in M0 (to fold into M1/M2)
62-
63-1. **Sandbox:**
64-   - Add a small *keeper* process with `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`. Without it a crashed host leaves the sandbox running; this was tested as a negative control.
65-   - Set `OOMPolicy=stop` and run `reset-failed` afterwards.
66-   - "Could not start" is decided by bwrap's `exit-code` record, not by `child-pid`.
67-   - PATH must put the toolchain's `bin/` first, never elan's proxies.
68-2. **Comparator messages.** A weakened goal abbrev is reported as "definition mismatch" against the abbrev's own name. The user- and LLM-facing message should say "a definition the frozen statement depends on changed".
69-3. **Claude CLI:**
70-   - Telelean's MCP tools need `alwaysLoad` and `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`, otherwise they hide behind a ToolSearch tool that isn't allowed.
71-   - Long questions need a per-server MCP timeout.
72-   - The account check uses the CLI's `initialize` reply before any prompt, so a refusal costs nothing.
73-   - In `-p` mode the CLI silently ignores an invalid settings file. Telelean therefore asks the running CLI for its hook list and refuses to start without the guard. The minimum CLI version is 2.1.295.
74-   - `--max-turns` counts per user turn, so telelean enforces its own run cap.
75-   - Haiku 5.5 can't switch thinking off in CLI 2.1.314; low effort keeps output short.
76-4. **Grep/Glob search hidden files.** The guard scans the search folder first. M1's shadow layout should give Claude a root holding only model files, with `.lake/` and `.telelean/` visible only inside the Lean sandbox.
77-5. **Board:**
78-   - Contributed colour ids must have exactly one dot. VS Code replaces only the first dot when naming the CSS variable.
79-   - Messages to a still-loading webview are queued, not dropped, so applying a graph must be idempotent or versioned.
80-   - Default colours should not rely on `charts.*` tokens, which some themes (e.g. Abyss) derive badly.
81-
82-## Open items (not blocking; M1/M2)
83-
84-- **runLean:**
85-  - production layout untested: a shadow under `~/.config`, and projects with real Lake dependencies;
86-  - G1's per-declaration budgets;
87-  - Lean errors are cut to their first line, which matters for the M2 retry prompts.
88-- **CLI:**
89-  - the hook has not been tested under the snap VS Code extension host;
90-  - a watchdog is needed if the extension host is SIGKILLed;
91-  - `check_lean` path validation, in the real host.
92-- **Board:** Undo, D-11 impact text on drop zones, keyboard equivalents, Shiki, persistence, vocabulary group.
93-- **Housekeeping:** 13 empty Chrome temp folders in `/tmp`, some older than this session, so not provably ours. Remove with `rmdir /tmp/com.google.Chrome.chrome_chrome_url_fetcher_.*` if you like.

- **A column-0 comment ends the declaration above it only when the next code after it starts a command (or there is none).** Lean treats comments as whitespace: a `--` or `/- -/` at column 0 inside a tactic proof or a multi-line statement, followed by more indented code, belongs to the declaration. The old rule cut such declarations in half, so D→A, A→G and delete broke files that compiled. *(fix)*
- **Two extra guards against cutting a declaration: `applyLeanOps` refuses when the line after a span is an indented continuation, and the planner refuses when Lean's own range of a freshly checked declaration ends after the span.** Defence in depth: a refusal ("edit it by hand") is always better than a half-removed proof. *(fix)*
- **Neighbouring declarations removed together are deleted in one piece.** One blank line stays where they were, not two. *(fix)*
- **Delete with its Lean asks first when other declarations would stop compiling, listing them (cards, then lemmas without a card and other subjects' proofs); the board resends with `confirmed: true`.** D-18 asks for a confirmation listing the dependents; the board alone sees only this subject's arrows. *(fix)*
- **D→A / G→A on a proof that takes hypotheses asks first; "rewrite" drops the arguments (`(n.holds h)` becomes `n.holds`), "mark broken" leaves them.** The axiom states `n` directly; the drop zone used to promise the proofs "stay valid" while they broke. Only direct users change (their own types do not). *(fix)*
- **A→G / D→G "rewrite" of a proof that takes hypotheses replaces each whole application `(n.holds h …)` by the new hypothesis `h_n : n`.** The user then rests on `n` and keeps its other hypotheses; replacing only the name gave `(h_n h)`, which does not compile. *(fix)*
- **The mechanical rewrite only touches applications in parentheses with plain identifiers as arguments (`(n.holds h)`, `((n.holds a) b)`); anything else is refused with "choose mark broken".** Recognising every way to apply a function is not worth the risk; the refusal names the place. *(fix)*
- **Lean's double references (`@c` with and without the `@`, `(c)` with and without its parentheses) are merged to one span per identifier, and a leading `@` is accepted.** Found with real `.ilean` files; the rewrite refused these harmless forms before. *(fix)*
- **While files are not freshly checked, a use counts when its name resolves through the declaration's namespaces or any namespace `open`ed earlier in the file, or when it ends with two or more components of the target (`cynder_dark_past.holds`).** Generous on purpose: one question too many is harmless, one missed use removes a `.holds` others use. *(fix)*
- **"Self-evident" requires no card and no hidden axiom in the footprint.** A proof resting on an unmarked axiom (TL103/TL104) is not proved from nothing. *(fix)*
- **A plan never changes another card's binding: a comment-only card left directly above a declaration gets a blank line after it; any other change is refused.** Deleting the card below it used to make it silently bind to that declaration. *(fix)*
- **Editing a field that a block repeats (TL005) changes only the first line and keeps the others; removing such a field is refused.** The later lines are text you typed; deleting them silently, or promoting a hidden one, would surprise. *(fix)*
- **A board lists the vocabulary items of other subjects that its cards use, read-only, under their full names.** Hover glosses and click-to-highlight then work for explicit imports (D-10). *(fix)*
- **graph.json 1.1: `conditional_on` holds a conditional proof's hypotheses and `footprint` its real footprint.** Scripts could not see what a conditional result rests on; the change is additive except for that field's meaning on conditional nodes (no outside users yet). *(fix)*
- **TL011 is worded like the card chip: "no source yet" for a rule, "no reason yet" otherwise; the impact text names the real hypothesis (`h_cynder_dark_past`).** The board and Problems now say the same thing. *(fix)*
- **Another toolchain, or a project M1 cannot check, drops the facts in use; the banner names the project's current pin.** D-7: the board must really be syntactic, as the banner says. *(fix)*
- **A revert refuses when the current state cannot be snapshotted first (actions still go ahead).** A revert deletes and overwrites hand-made files; A3 promises they are snapshotted first. An ordinary action keeps the hand edits in the files. *(fix)*
- **Of a subject's sidecar folder, history covers only `layout.json` and `attic/*.lean`.** Other files (a picture) would be corrupted by being read as text; now they are never snapshotted, reverted or deleted. *(fix)*

- **A linked git worktree gets its own history chains (`-wt<hash>` in the ref key); the main worktree keeps its key.** Refs are shared by all worktrees; two checkouts at the same path mixed their histories. *(fix)*
- **Blocks carry their namespace from the parser; the model builder's per-block scans use binary search.** The model was rebuilt in quadratic time (6 s for 1600 cards in one file); now 18 ms. *(fix)*
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# RAM watchdog (turn 2). Warn < 12 GB available, critical < 4 GB.
# On critical, kills ONLY processes started for this work: telelean-* systemd scopes,
# VS Code *test* instances (.vscode-test), and anything whose cwd is in my scratchpad.
SCR=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad
state=ok
while true; do
  avail=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  if [ "$avail" -lt 4096 ]; then
    if [ "$state" != crit ]; then
      echo "CRITICAL: MemAvailable ${avail} MB — killing my own test/build processes"
      systemctl --user kill 'telelean-*' 2>/dev/null
      pkill -f '\.vscode-test/' 2>/dev/null
      for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do c=$(readlink "$p/cwd" 2>/dev/null); case "$c" in "$SCR"*) kill "${p#/proc/}" 2>/dev/null;; esac; done
      state=crit
    fi
  elif [ "$avail" -lt 12288 ]; then
    [ "$state" = ok ] && echo "WARN: MemAvailable ${avail} MB"
    state=warn
  else
    [ "$state" != ok ] && echo "RECOVERED: MemAvailable ${avail} MB"
    state=ok
  fi
  sleep 5
done

/*
 * Static harness for the telelean board bundle. It provides what VS Code and the extension give a webview:
 *  - the --vscode-* theme variables and body classes (approximations of Dark Modern, Light Modern, High Contrast);
 *  - a mock acquireVsCodeApi() that records every posted message in window.__tlHarness.posted;
 *  - getState/setState kept in sessionStorage, so the webview state survives page.reload() as it survives a webview
 *    reload in VS Code;
 *  - a minimal host: "ready" is answered with window.__TL_HARNESS__.workspace (if any) and then .graph; every
 *    mutating message with a requestId gets an actionResult (ok, with outcome.nodeId = clientId for addNode, unless a
 *    queued reply says otherwise); historyList gets the canned listing (.history); copyText gets a "Copied" notice.
 * URL parameter: ?theme=dark|light|hc
 * window.__TL_HARNESS__ (set by the Playwright test before the page loads):
 *   graph       the TlGraph sent after "ready"
 *   workspace   optional WorkspaceState sent after "ready", before the graph

#!/bin/sh
# Logs MemAvailable every 5 s; below 4 GiB it kills the process groups listed in pgids.txt (only my own test runs).
S=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad/turn9/closing-fixer-r1
touch $S/pgids.txt
while [ -f $S/watchdog.on ]; do
  avail=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) MemAvailable=${avail}MB" >> $S/watchdog.log
  if [ "$avail" -lt 4096 ]; then
    echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) LOW MEMORY: killing my process groups: $(cat $S/pgids.txt | tr '\n' ' ')" >> $S/watchdog.log
    for g in $(cat $S/pgids.txt); do kill -TERM -- -$g 2>/dev/null; done
  fi
  sleep 5
done
EOF

import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import { mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { chromeTmpDir } from './test/harness/chrome-tmp';

const PORT = 41739;

/**
 * Chrome's environment: ours, with TMPDIR, HOME and the XDG base directories all inside this run's short temp
 * directory (see test/harness/chrome-tmp.ts), so nothing Chrome writes (profile, crash reports, NSS database,
 * caches) lands in the real home folder; the global teardown deletes the directory. test/harness/home-guard.ts
 * checks the real home folder afterwards (docs/m1-plan.md section 10).
 */
function chromeEnv(): Record<string, string> {
  const tmp = chromeTmpDir();
  const dirs = { HOME: join(tmp, 'home'), XDG_CONFIG_HOME: join(tmp, 'xdg-config'), XDG_CACHE_HOME: join(tmp, 'xdg-cache'), XDG_DATA_HOME: join(tmp, 'xdg-data') };
  for (const dir of Object.values(dirs)) mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  return {
    ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter((entry): entry is [string, string] => entry[1] !== undefined)),
    TMPDIR: tmp,
    ...dirs,
  };
}

/**
 * Browser tests of the built bundle (packages/extension/dist/webview) in a static harness page with a mock
 * acquireVsCodeApi. Uses the installed Google Chrome (channel "chrome"); never downloads browsers.
 * One worker: one browser at a time (RAM rule). The npm script runs it under `ulimit -c 0` (no core dumps).

  // Screenshots are written to test-results/ directly; Playwright's own artifacts go one level down so the

  outputDir: 'test-results/playwright',
  workers: 1,
  fullyParallel: false,
  retries: 0,
  timeout: 30_000,

  reporter: [['list']],
  globalSetup: './test/harness/home-guard.ts',

name: Bash
desc: Update decisions log sections 12 and 13
cmd:
cd /home/zhengyew/telelean/docs && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='decisions-log.md'
s=open(p).read()
rep=[]
rep.append(("""fix = the fixers after the verification (section 10 lists the core and runner ones, section 11 the extension and webview ones, section 12 the closing round).""","""fix = the fixers after the verification (section 10 lists the core and runner ones, section 11 the extension and webview ones, sections 12 and 13 the two closing rounds)."""))
rep.append(("""- **A dependent the board cannot show by its sentence (a lemma without a card, a card of another subject) is shown by its name in code font.** The board only has this subject's cards; the host's message names the other subjects' cards, but parsing it would be fragile. *(fix)*""","""- **A dependent the board cannot show by its sentence is shown in code font: a lemma without a card by its Lean name, a card of another subject by its card id.** The board only has this subject's cards; the host's message names the other subjects' cards, but parsing it would be fragile. *(fix; superseded in round 2, section 13: the host now describes those cards, so another subject's card shows by its sentence)*"""))
for old,new in rep:
    assert s.count(old)==1, old[:80]
    s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.rstrip('\n')+"""

## 13. Closing fixes (round 2)

- **The end-to-end suite clears VS Code's own notification toasts: before its first test it waits (at most 20 s) for the startup toast "All installed extensions are temporarily disabled" and clears it, and before every test it clears any toast still shown. `--disable-extensions` stays in the test instances' launch arguments.** That toast is sticky and urgent (do-not-disturb does not hide it) and covers the board's bottom-right corner, so the click on the A|D|G box's Add button failed whenever the toast came first (every run on the verifier's machine). Dropping the flag would also avoid it, but the flag is part of the planned isolation (`docs/m1-plan.md` section 10): it keeps every installed extension out even if the isolated extensions folder were ever wrong. *(fix)*
- **The end-to-end delete test waits until Main.lean and layout.json both show the delete, and builds the expected layout from the layout as it was before the delete (it no longer requires that earlier tests put the card in the layout).** The applier saves layout.json about 100 ms after Main.lean, and one failed earlier test made this one fail too. *(fix)*
- **A `needs-confirmation` answer names the cards among its dependents, in any subject (`dependentCards`: id → subject, kind, sentence), added by the extension host from the subjects' graphs; the dialogs show another subject's card as its kind letter, its sentence and "(subject …)", and anything else by its Lean name in code font.** The board's graph holds only its own subject's cards, so another subject's card showed as its raw id, which looks like a Lean name but is neither its sentence nor its Lean name. *(fix)*
- **The kind-change preview (drop zones, the **Make …** tooltips, the "why" dialog) says "No card on this board uses it" instead of "Nothing uses it".** The preview is computed from the board's graph alone, so it cannot know about lemmas without a card; the host's question that may follow no longer contradicts it. *(fix)*
- **Core's refusal to delete Lean code agrees in number: "breaks a declaration that uses it (…), which stops compiling" for one dependent.** It shows in the extension log and in the rare toasts for this refusal. *(fix)*
- **A file-watcher event reads the file once and matches its text against telelean's recent writes and the user's handled saves before either forgets: only the source it matches records the match; when none matches, both forget.** Otherwise a save's echo, handled after telelean wrote the same file, made telelean's own write look like another program's (one redundant Lean refresh). *(fix)*
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
tail -9 decisions-log.md | cut -c1-150
